title: Two Ledgers, One Gate
summary: This is the round-1 'Two Ledgers, One Gate' you picked, with 'Built for' and 'Not for' now set as large 42px headings you can't miss. B's spine is redrawn as one precise C-style line: it enters at the left, passes through the audit gate and forks, solid up to Built for and dashed down to Not for.

reference.site: Round 1 · B (Two Ledgers, One Gate) + C's drafting precision (Fit Check Sheet)
reference.borrowed: From B, the report's chapter-opener structure behind your round-1 pick. Two stacked hairline ledgers hang from a spine, each row opens in place with one row open per ledger, and the doors close the list as its last row. From C (Speakeasy's framed comparison, as drawn in the Fit Check Sheet): mirrored Fit / Decline lists whose rows pair up by axis, F- and D- mono IDs, coded callouts on straight leaders and a small title block.
reference.kelwin: The head is the shared A grammar: '■ Who it’s for' with 'Fig. 09' at the right (as on every other section), the two-voice 88px 'Not for everyone. / We qualify first.', the 48×2 red rule and the lede, with the quiet note '■ Strict qualification' bottom-left, level with the doors (the hero's diagonal). B's spine becomes the TRACE primitive in its fork variant (DIRECTION-AC P1). One 1px ink line enters at the left margin (callout 01 'Every engagement'), shows its direction with one open chevron, and passes through the gate: two posts across the line with the gate node seated between them (callout 02 'The audit'). On the col 4|5 gutter it forks: solid up to Built for, dashed (2 4) down to Not for. Each branch turns and becomes its ledger's top rule, so the headings literally sit on their branch. The Built-for end node is filled (admitted); the Not-for end node stays open (declined). The ledger headings change from 11px mono captions to 42px wide display (.ac-h3--lg), set flush on the ledger's left edge, with a plain sub ('We say yes when' / 'We decline when') and a count. The rows are mirrored by axis, so F-02 'Ready to own the system' pairs with D-02 'Lead-list shopping', and those two rest open. One title block (FIG. 09 · One gate · Two branches). Red appears only on the primary button, plus the label squares and the rule. No logo geometry, no ruler and no day count (method, directly above, owns the ruler).

addressed: 'Built for' and 'Not for' are now large 42px headings in the same wide face as the statement, where they used to be tiny tracked mono captions. Each sits flush on the left edge of its list with a plain sub ('We say yes when' / 'We decline when') and a count, so you can tell the two lists apart at a glance.

Option C's precision comes in as one drawing, not as clutter: a single line enters at the left, passes through the audit gate and forks into the two lists. The yes branch is solid and the no branch is dashed, and each branch becomes the top rule of its list.

Other C details, each used once: two coded callouts (01 Every engagement · 02 The audit), F-01 / D-01 IDs with rows paired by axis, and one small title block. No cell grids, spec tables, rulers or mono sentences.
Kept as you liked it: the two stacked ledgers that open in place with one row open each, the muted Not-for list, your round-1 copy and 'Sound like you?' with both doors as the closing row.

The motion tells the story in reading order: the gate is drafted first, the line draws through it and the nodes latch as it passes. Then it forks up and down, the branches draw across as the headings rise, and the rows follow. A single signal then travels the yes path to Built for.

Fits the blended system: the head matches the hero, the nav and its neighbours (label, 'Fig. 09', two-voice statement, red rule, quiet note bottom-left, red button + underlined link). There is no logo symbol anywhere, and the only red beyond the label squares and rule is the primary button.

Final coherence pass: the red rule now sits 36px under the headline, exactly as in every other section (it had drifted to 56px). The lists keep their place, so 'Built for' still clears the headline, and your lede's first line now lines up with the 'Built for' heading.
motion: entrance (kit head): the label fades in, 'Not for everyone.' then the light 'We qualify first.' rise out of their masks, the 48×2 red rule draws (520ms) and the lede fades up 12px (600ms).

the orchestrated moment (TRACE · fork, drafting order): the construction comes first. The two gate posts draw from their centres (440–860ms), and the five nodes appear as 7px outlines. From 600ms the line plots left to right from node 01 (800ms, --ease-inout, clip-path draw), and its one chevron fades in as the line passes (900ms). Each node latches from outline to filled (200ms) as the line reaches it: 01 at 620ms, the gate at 1.0s and the fork at 1.4s. The callouts fade in behind the line (01 at 700ms, 02 at 1.08s), then the title block (1.3s). At 1.4s the line forks: the solid arm climbs to Built for (450ms) while the short dashed arm drops to Not for (300ms), so both corners land together at 1.85s. The Built-for node latches filled and the Not-for node stays open. Both branches then draw across as the ledgers' top rules (700ms) while 'Built for' / 'Not for' rise out of their masks (1.86s / 1.96s). The rows cascade in reading order (F-01 → F-03 from 2.0s, D-01 → D-03 from 2.24s, 80ms stagger), and the closing row with both doors and the bottom-left note rises at 2.6s. At 3.0s the Not-for ledger opens D-02 'Lead-list shopping' in place (360ms, + turns to −), mirroring the open F-02 'Ready to own the system'.

ambient (the one loop): a 6px ink packet leaves node 01 at 1.9s and travels the yes path (trunk → gate → fork → up to Built for) at constant speed in 2.6s. It fades as it reaches the latched Built-for node, rests, and runs again every 8s.

interaction: each ledger opens in place, one row at a time (the kit's + rotates to −, 360ms --ease-inout), and clicking the open row closes it. Hovering a row nudges its title 6px right, and a Not-for title goes from muted to ink on hover or when open. The first click stops the timed demo. The primary button uses --accent-hover with an up-right nudge on its ↗, and the secondary link's underline goes to ink and its → nudges right.

on the live site: the fork plays once when the figure is 40% visible (IntersectionObserver, no pin), and D-02 opens once after both ledgers land. The packet loop starts only after the fork has drawn and pauses when the section leaves view. Reduced motion renders the final drawing from the markup synchronously (both ledgers with F-02 / D-02 open, every node latched except the open Not-for end), with no packet and no timers.
notes: Stage is 1380px tall (kit 128px padding, 88px head, 42px set headings on fixed 76px bands). The fork is layout-driven, not measured: it spans from the Built-for rule to the Not-for rule (both sit at a fixed band height), and the trunk enters mid-gap between the two ledgers (--tj), so it never lines up with a row hairline and holds in the Kelwin skin too. Only the ambient packet reads positions in JS. C quotas: 1 drawing, 2 callouts (≤ 4 words each), 0 dimension lines, 0 registration marks, 1 title block of 3 cells, about 9 annotation words, 5 nodes, 1 chevron, mono lines ≤ 22 characters and none of them a sentence. Review pass (round 2): the '10 working days' dimension and its ruler-like posts were removed because method X, directly above, leads with the same ruler and the same '10 working days' label (and the CTA owns the ten-tick ruler); the boxed + / − beside the headings were removed because the same glyphs already mean 'open this row' at the right of every row, so they read as buttons; the label-row meta now reads 'Fig. 09' like every sibling section. The ledger's own top border is made transparent because the TRACE branch draws that edge (the same approach as faq-X). Copy is round-1 B's, with em dashes turned into sentences. The Not-for rows are reordered to mirror their Fit pair by axis (stage · ownership · motion), following round-1 C. Final coherence pass: the left column's rule is pulled up 20px (margin only) so the head keeps the page's 36 / 28 rule rhythm, while the ledgers stay at 56px below the statement.
